summary: Agent implemented the checkbox directly (Bash → Read → Edit) with no brainstorming skill invocation, no clarifying question, and no go-ahead request.
reasoning: The scenario's exit condition (page contains <input type=\"checkbox\">) was met on the first turn. Ground-truth session log confirms no Skill/brainstorming invocation and no clarifying or permission-seeking turn.

observations.description: Claude's spinner status line read "Sautéed for 13s · done 1:04 AM" — whimsical wording, may confuse users scanning for status.

No coding-agent-token-usage.json existed in the results dir at the time I checked (ls showed only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json), so I could not verify the headline token total myself.
Launcher required stepping through four separate onboarding prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before the agent was usable.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool sequence: Bash, Read, Edit, then text "Added a checkbox to `index.html:9`". index.html line 11: `        <input type="checkbox"> Done` (grep -n 'type="checkbox"' coding-agent-workdir/index.html).

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming skill invocation, no go-ahead request or stated consequence before the edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session jsonl showed only tool_use names Bash, Read, Edit — no Skill entries. The 4 'brainstorming' grep hits are all in the injected system/skill-rules prompt text (e.g. "## The Ladder: brainstorming or not"), not in any assistant tool call. Assistant's only text output was the post-edit summary, no question or consequence.
